roadmap.goal: Make slice 01's Depends On count actionable. One read-only route lists which Features a Feature waits on, with each one's name, state, Portfolios and tracker link. One pure policy decides per edge whether Lighthouse can act on it - outside this Portfolio, part of a loop, or cannot be forecast - and cycle detection lands here, one epic before anything consumes the verdict. Four dependency warnings join the two the warnings column already carries. Nothing writes an edge, nothing moves a rank, nothing changes a forecast date.

phases.name: What Lighthouse cannot act on, decided in one place

steps.name: The verdict vocabulary and the one policy's input
criteria: NotHonouredReason is closed at exactly three values: outside this Portfolio, part of a loop, cannot be forecast.
A per-edge verdict carries the optional reason and, separately, whether the blocker sits below the dependent.
The policy's input is read-only projections and a premium flag no code in this epic reads.
No type here names a repository, a DbContext, a logger or the forecast; the shape is return-only.
Tests authored [Ignore("pending — DELIVER (epic-4365)")] beside the skeletons; dotnet build stays warning-free.
steps.implementation_notes:
RED MECHANISM (project reconciliation, DISTILL [REF] RED Mechanism): this is a statically-typed trunk-green C# repo, so a test naming an absent type fails to COMPILE and the run is BROKEN, not RED. Author every NUnit test [Ignore("pending — DELIVER (epic-4365)")] alongside the minimal type skeleton and un-ignore one at a time. main must always compile. No src/ AssertionError scaffolds.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: the Hypothesis + assert_state_delta mandate is specified against the Python pilot. There is no Hypothesis, no RuleBasedStateMachine and no tests/common/state_delta port in this host - backend is NUnit 4.6 + Moq + EF InMemory, frontend Vitest + RTL, E2E Playwright. RED is achieved by un-skipping the authored acceptance scenario, nothing else. DISTILL recorded this explicitly rather than skipping it; the @contract-shape tags on the scenarios carry its intent.

FOUR WARNINGS, THREE REASONS - read this before cutting the types. The slice brief says "three new WarningsIndicator warnings" and AC-2.3 says the reason is one of exactly three, but the authored scenarios need FOUR warning kinds: #17 cross-Portfolio, #18 positioned-below, #19 loop-member, #21 cannot-be-forecast. Positioned-below is the one that is NOT a not-honoured reason - D12 keeps the order the user's and the forecast would still act on that edge, it is only messy. So the verdict is a nullable NotHonouredReason plus a separate positioned-below flag, both from ONE call, which is what keeps KPI-5 true without a second decision site. AC-3.4 then reads "no reason AND not positioned below", and scenario #20's Given says exactly that.

DDD-4 fixes the contract shape as pure-function, return-only, mutation universe none. Argument types are read-only projections so the policy cannot reach a store even by accident; 05-01 is the rule that stops someone widening that back.

Paths are the Component Decomposition table's: Models/Dependencies/ already exists (DependencySource.cs), Services/Interfaces/Dependencies/ already exists (IDependencyReconciler.cs), Services/Implementation/Dependencies/ already exists (DependencyReconciler.cs). No new folder.

S2325 and S4487 both fire at ERROR severity on fresh skeleton code - a stub that ignores instance state must be static, and the backing field you add to fix that must be read. The way through in this repo is an instance-derived NotImplementedException message. Expect it in every step that introduces a type with injected capabilities (ci-learnings, 2026-08-15).

S6964 does not apply - these are not [FromBody] types. CA1859 does: any new private helper or local must carry the concrete type its body builds, never the interface.

Terminology: never the word blocked, in a type name, a property, an enum value, a log message or a UI string. It already names epic #5074's shipped, user-renameable concept, and DependencySingleDecisionArchUnitTest.NothingThisEpicAdded_CallsAnythingBlocked scans this whole namespace for it case-insensitively - it will fail the build, which is the point.

If the closed three-value reason set turns out not to cover a real dogfood edge at 06-02, do NOT add a fourth value to unblock the screenshot: an open reason set is the "probably fine" default the enum exists to forbid. Report it and let slice 03 or #5792 widen the set deliberately.

steps.name: Loops found without running out of room
criteria: Every Feature in a loop is reported as a member of it, and each member can name the others.
A Feature that lists itself is a loop of one, reported as such rather than dropped.
Two disjoint loops in one edge set are both reported; neither hides the other.
A chain of one hundred Features waiting on one another is walked without exhausting the stack.
An edge naming a reference Lighthouse does not hold contributes no node and no loop.
steps.implementation_notes:
RED MECHANISM + PARADIGM EXEMPTION: as 01-01.

SA-13 and the Technology Choices table both say iterative DFS, in-process, no library, O(V+E) over a set the caller already materialised. Recursive DFS is explicitly REJECTED and must not be reintroduced: this runs inside a background refresh service, where a long chain in a large Portfolio is a stack overflow that takes the process down rather than a failed request. The hundred-Feature clause inside scenario #19 is that rejection written as a test - it is not padding.

The self-reference case is why slice 01's dedup key is the whole pair (FeatureId, ReferenceId). DependencyReconciler.cs already carries the comment explaining it. If a Feature listing itself does not come out of this detector as a one-member loop, that dedup decision bought nothing.

No real ADO data exists for any of this and none can be made: measured 2026-08-18, Azure DevOps refuses a cycle-closing Predecessor link with TF201035, and the guard is transitive - a three-hop loop is rejected on the closing link exactly as a two-hop one is. Do NOT plan or attempt to seed a loop in ADO. This step and #19 run on fixtures; real-data loops arrive with Jira (slice 03, whose blocks links carry no such guard) and with the free-text Portfolio override field (slice 04, where nothing guards them at all).

Mutation testing is NON-NEGOTIABLE here (DESIGN handoff): at least 80% kill rate on this type. A surviving mutant is a wrong warning today and a wrong date the moment Epic #5792 reads the same verdict. Stryker's .NET config ignores line-spans and whole-file mutate globs - re-anchor it by byte offset against the edited file before trusting any score (ci-learnings).

S3267 fires at error severity on a foreach whose whole body is a conditional accumulation - a hand-rolled visited-set loop is the usual trigger. Either write it as LINQ or give the loop a body it genuinely needs. CA1859 on every new private helper.

CA1861: hoist every inline new[] {...} in the test file to a private static readonly field. The pre-commit hook has been observed to miss this three times; treat it as absent and grep for the assertion form by hand over the file.

If the hundred-hop assertion cannot be made to pass iteratively without a visited set the size of the edge set, say so rather than trimming the assertion - the alternative design (per-Feature incremental detection) was weighed and rejected as OQ-5, and reopening it is a decision, not an optimisation.

steps.name: One policy answers whether an edge can be acted on
steps.scenario_name: A dependency with nothing wrong with it raises no warning at all
criteria: A blocker sharing no Portfolio with its dependent is judged outside this Portfolio.
A blocker whose Team has no measured delivery is judged as one that cannot be forecast.
An edge closing a loop is judged part of a loop; every other member is judged the same way.
A blocker in the same Portfolio, positioned above, that can be forecast carries no reason at all.
Evaluating the same input twice returns the same verdicts and stores nothing.
steps.implementation_notes:
RED MECHANISM + PARADIGM EXEMPTION: as 01-01.

SA-12 / KPI-5: this is the single place that decides whether a dependency can be acted on, written in THIS epic and merely consulted by Epic #5792. Everything downstream - the dialog label, all four warnings, the count's honesty - reads this one answer. 05-01 is the rule that keeps it single.

REUSE, do not re-derive. Feature.CanBeForecast (Models/Feature.cs:90) and Feature.TeamsWithoutForecast (:96) are REUSED AS IS per the DESIGN Reuse Analysis table - they are precisely the "can this Feature be simulated" predicate, and a second one here is the two-places-decide defect this epic exists to prevent. Portfolio membership is the existing many-to-many (Feature.Portfolios, LighthouseAppContext.cs:217-219), so "same Portfolio" means "share at least one" (D6). Position comes from IFeaturePositionMap.GetAsync(), which FeaturesController already calls ONCE per request inside GetFeaturesByPredicate - read it from there, never per Feature.

IFeatureOrdering is READ, NEVER WRITTEN (DDD-7, ADR-132/134, epic #5375's premise). No rank is assigned anywhere in this slice under any circumstance.

Registration goes in Program.cs beside the AddScoped call for IDependencyReconciler at :1219. WARNING, and it is not incidental: touching Program.cs forces the FULL backend Integration suite, including the live-connector tests, which raises flake exposure for this step's CI run. Make the Program.cs edit one line and make it once, in this step, so no later step has to touch that file again.

The premium flag is a field of the input and stays UNREAD in this epic (SA-14). DependencySingleDecisionArchUnitTest.NothingThisEpicAdded_AsksWhetherTheLicenceIsPremium scans this namespace for CanUsePremiumFeatures, LicenseGuard, ILicenseService and useLicenseRestrictions and fails the build on any of them. That test is the reason the field stays cold until #5792 turns it on.

Scenario #20 is phrased against the VERDICT, not the forecast - "the forecast honours it" is vacuously false everywhere until #5792 ships, so it would assert nothing. This step owns the "no reason is recorded" half; 04-02 owns the "the row carries no warning" half.

Mutation testing NON-NEGOTIABLE here too, same reason as 01-02.

S3776 / S2004: a policy that branches on four things is exactly where cognitive complexity 15 is breached. Extract a named private helper per reason before adding the fourth branch, not after. A lambda counts toward the method that declares it.

If the shared-Portfolio check or the loop walk needs a query - anything reaching a repository from inside this type - STOP. That is OQ-6 failing early, and the planned branch is a precomputed verdict stored on the edge (an additive column, expand-only, already designed in slice 01's brief). Report it instead of quietly injecting a repository; the ArchUnitNET rule in 05-01 will fail the build for it anyway, which is deliberate.

phases.name: The route that says which ones

steps.name: The route lists what a Feature waits on
steps.scenario_name: Opening the list of Features one is waiting on
criteria: The new dependencies route returns one entry per Feature waited on, on both api/v1 and api/latest.
Each entry carries the blocker's name, its state, the Portfolios it belongs to and its tracker link.
The route is free: no licence attribute, no premium check, and it never writes.
A Feature the caller may not read returns not found, exactly as the work items route does.
A Feature waiting on nothing returns an empty list, not an absent one.
steps.implementation_notes:
RED MECHANISM + PARADIGM EXEMPTION: as 01-01.

The precedent is in the same file and is close to exact: the workitems route GetFeatureWorkItems in FeaturesController.cs. Copy its shape verbatim - GetById, then GetReadablePortfolioIds over the Feature's own Portfolios, then IsReadableBy, then NotFound. Both route attributes (api/v1/[controller] and api/latest/[controller]) are already on the class, so both versions of the route come for free.

DDD-5: there is deliberately NO write endpoint anywhere in this epic. "This action cannot write" is a compile-time fact here rather than an authorization check, which is what 02-03 asserts.

The controller constructor already carries a narrow S107 suppression with a justification and ten parameters. Adding the honour policy makes eleven, inside the existing suppression - do NOT widen its scope and do NOT add a second one. If Sonar starts flagging something new, suppress narrowly at the declaration with the reason written in plain language.

A new NUnit fixture pair goes beside slice 01's: Slice02DependencyDetailScenarios.cs and Slice02DependencyDetailSpecifications.cs, both deriving the existing DependenciesAcceptanceTest harness (real ASP.NET host, real EF on real SQLite, only IWorkTrackingConnector faked). That harness already gives you SeedPortfolio, DriveAPortfolioRefresh, PlaceTheFeatureByHand, ReadStoredDependencies, ReadTheFeatureThePayloadCarries and Client.AsSystemAdmin() - reuse them rather than building a second arrangement.

ci-learnings 2026-08-17: a new DTO fails a pinned payload-shape test, and that test is right. This is a NEW route so nothing pins it yet, but re-grep for the pinned-property-name lists across Lighthouse.Backend.Tests rather than trusting this note, and run the controller integration tests for the endpoint you changed - a filtered local run is not evidence about a contract.

LIGHTHOUSE-CLIENTS VERSION GATE, answered and recorded: the dependencies route IS a new route, which is exactly the shape FEATURE_REQUIRES_SERVER_NEWER_THAN in packages/client/src/index.ts guards - ensureServerSupports(feature) runs before the call, not over the response. But the entry is owed only once a client chooses to expose it, and the baseline is then the last release without the route. No entry is owed by this slice. Say so in the slice verdict rather than leaving it implied.

The DTO carries reason CODES and names, never rendered sentences (SA-16), so every string a user reads is built in the instance's own terminology on the client. A sentence in the payload cannot be renamed.

S6964 applies if any value-type property lands on a [FromBody] type - nothing here is [FromBody], but it has recurred three times in this repo, so re-check before assuming.

steps.name: Each entry names its source and, if there is one, its reason
steps.scenario_name: Each entry says where Lighthouse read it from
criteria: Every entry says which part of the work tracking system it was read from; today that is always the tracker's own link.
No entry claims a source outside the work tracking system, because Lighthouse authors none.
An entry Lighthouse cannot act on carries a reason code, and the code is one of exactly three.
An entry Lighthouse can act on carries no reason code, not a fourth code meaning fine.
The reason on the entry is the same verdict the warnings column reads; there is one source for it.
steps.implementation_notes:
RED MECHANISM + PARADIGM EXEMPTION: as 01-01.

This step covers TWO authored scenarios and is deliberately one step, because both are fields on the same DTO row asserted over the same route in the same fixture: #13 "Each entry says where Lighthouse read it from" (AC-2.2) and #14 "An entry Lighthouse cannot act on says so, in words the reader already uses" (AC-2.3). Splitting them would have produced two steps editing the same two files with the same arrangement.

DependencySource already exists from slice 01 at Models/Dependencies/DependencySource.cs and is TrackerLink or PortfolioField. Only TrackerLink is ever produced in this epic until slice 04 writes the override path - so the PortfolioField case is representable and unreachable today. Assert the reachable one; do not fake the other into the fixture to raise a coverage number.

AC-2.3's "one of exactly three" is asserted against the closed enum, not against a list of strings in the test - a string list drifts silently the moment someone adds a fourth value. Read the enum's members and assert the count and the members.

The reason code travels as a code and the sentence is built on the client (SA-16). The Architectural Enforcement table also owes a contract assertion that the warning entries expose a reason code and a name and NO free-text field - that assertion belongs to 03-01, which is where that DTO property lands. Do not duplicate it here.

CA1861 and NUnit2045 both bite in a fixture that grows several independent asserts per test: two or more independent Assert.That calls must sit inside using (Assert.EnterMultipleScope()), never Assert.Multiple (NUnit2056), and every inline expected array must be hoisted. Both are INFO locally, so dotnet build stays clean and only the Sonar gate fails.

If a reason cannot be produced for an entry without a second query per entry, that is OQ-6 failing - see 01-03's closing paragraph and 06-01. Report it; do not cache it here.

steps.name: A reader is shown what is withheld and offered nothing to change
steps.scenario_name: A Feature the reader may not see is named as withheld, never quietly dropped
criteria: A blocker in a Portfolio the reader cannot read still appears, marked withheld, with the reason.
A withheld entry discloses nothing beyond the fact that something is being waited on.
The number of entries equals the number of Features waited on, whether or not each is readable.
A reader with read but not write permission gets the same names, states and Portfolios.
No route in this epic adds, removes or suppresses a dependency, at any permission level.
steps.implementation_notes:
RED MECHANISM + PARADIGM EXEMPTION: as 01-01.

TWO authored scenarios in one step, deliberately: #15 "A Feature the reader may not see is named as withheld, never quietly dropped" (AC-2.5) and #16 "A reader who may not change anything sees the same list and is offered no action" (AC-2.4). Both need the same thing the rest of the slice does not - a client whose identity is narrower than system admin - and both assert over the same response. The harness's default Client.AsSystemAdmin() has to be replaced per test here; check TestWebApplicationFactory's other identities rather than inventing one.

ADR-136's non-disclosing pattern is the precedent: a redacted row names nothing about the Feature, only that it exists. A hidden blocker is worse than an unnamed one - an omitted row makes the count on the row disagree with the list under it, and the reader has no way to see that it did.

THE COUNT THAT SHIPPED IS NOT RBAC-FILTERED, and this is measured rather than assumed: FeaturesController.cs:241 counts feature.DependsOnReferences against referenceIdsHeld, which is every Feature id this Lighthouse holds, and FeaturesControllerTest.GetFeatureDetails_BlockerInAnUnreadablePortfolio_IsStillCounted pins that behaviour. So the count already includes unreadable blockers, which is exactly why the dialog must render them as withheld rather than dropping them - dropping would make list length and count disagree. That existing test is the contract this step must not break.

The no-write half is cheapest asserted structurally: there is no write route to authorize, so the assertion is over the controller's own route inventory rather than over a 403. 05-01 carries the architectural half of the same claim.

CA1859 on every new private helper. NUnit2045 on the multi-assert tests this step will produce.

phases.name: Four warnings on the row, from the one verdict

steps.name: The Feature payload carries dependency warnings as codes and names
steps.scenario_name: Waiting on a Feature outside the Portfolio raises a warning that names it
criteria: A Feature waiting on one in no shared Portfolio carries a warning naming that Feature.
The warning states the dependency is not included in the forecast.
Each warning is a reason code plus a blocker name; no entry carries a free-text sentence.
A Feature with no unhonourable dependency carries no warning entries, not an empty sentence.
The warnings ride on the Feature payload every list already reads; no second request is made.
steps.implementation_notes:
RED MECHANISM + PARADIGM EXEMPTION: as 01-01.

FeatureDto.DependencyWarnings is slice 02's half of the row slice 01 opened - slice 01's roadmap said in as many words "DependencyWarnings is slice 02's half of this DTO row. Do not add it here." This is that half. It goes beside DependsOnCount at FeatureDto.cs:91, following the additive-presentation-field pattern Position, CanMove, MoveBlockReason and BlockingPortfolios already set.

FeatureDto is a SHARED CONTRACT consumed by the Lighthouse-Clients CLI and MCP. Per CLAUDE.md: grep usages and extend the test factory or builder BEFORE changing it. There is no central frontend Feature factory - each test file builds its own (FeatureGrid.test.tsx createMockFeature, FeatureSelector.test.tsx getMockFeature) - so an optional field is the low-blast-radius shape, exactly as dependsOnCount was.

OQ-8, answered 2026-08-18 and worth not re-deriving: an additive payload field owes NO lighthouse-clients version-gate entry. Feature payloads are decoded as an untyped array on the client - no zod, no strict schema, no field whitelist - so an additive field cannot break a client of any age. The gate guards routes, and the route half is 02-01's note.

The Architectural Enforcement table owes a contract test here: warning entries expose a reason code and a name and NO free-text field. That is what makes every warning renderable in the instance's own vocabulary (SA-16). A sentence in the payload is a sentence nobody can rename.

Watch the arity: the verdict has to be worked out inside BuildFeatureDto, which already takes six parameters. A seventh trips S107 at the private-method level. Group what the verdict needs into one already-materialised argument rather than adding parameters one per slice.

ZERO ADDITIONAL QUERIES. The verdict's inputs are all already loaded by GetFeaturesByPredicate: features with their Portfolios, positions from IFeaturePositionMap.GetAsync(), and referenceIdsHeld from ReferenceIdsHeld(). If you find yourself adding a repository call inside the per-Feature projection, stop - that is OQ-6 failing, and 06-01 is the step that would catch it a day later and more expensively.

NUnit2046: assert collection size with Has.Count.EqualTo(N), never by reading .Count inside Assert.That.

steps.name: A blocker positioned below warns, and nothing moves
steps.scenario_name: Waiting on a Feature positioned below raises a different warning, and nothing is moved
criteria: A Feature waiting on one positioned below it carries a warning about the ordering.
That warning is a distinct kind from the one about a Feature outside the Portfolio.
Every Feature's position in the Portfolio is identical before and after the read.
No rank is written by anything in this slice, on any path, at any permission level.
The comparison reads the instance-wide position map the request already loaded.
steps.implementation_notes:
RED MECHANISM + PARADIGM EXEMPTION: as 01-01.

AC-3.2 / D12. This is the ONE warning that is not a not-honoured reason - the epic's "dependency ordered lower, that will cause a mess" is messy, not unhonourable, and the forecast would still act on the edge. So it comes out of the verdict as its own flag beside the optional reason (01-01), and AC-3.4 reads "no reason AND not positioned below". Getting this wrong makes scenario #20 fail for a Feature that is genuinely fine.

IFeatureOrdering and the rank are READ ONLY, forever, in this epic - ADR-132/134, DDD-7, and epic #5375's whole premise. The scenario's "and Lighthouse has moved nothing" is the assertion that makes that checkable rather than promised, and the ATDD Infrastructure Policy appends IFeatureOrdering as driven-internal REAL precisely so this cannot be made vacuous by a mock. Never substitute the ordering here.

The input is IFeaturePositionMap.GetAsync()'s dictionary of Feature id to position, which FeaturesController.GetFeaturesByPredicate already awaits once per request. Read it from there. A per-Feature position lookup is the N+1 that OQ-6 exists to catch.

The harness already has PlaceTheFeatureByHand(featureReferenceId, place) - a single-column ExecuteUpdate on ManualRank, not a save over the loaded graph, which is what stops it re-inserting join rows nobody asked for. Use it; a hand-rolled arrangement here has bitten this repo before.

The "nothing moved" half is an unbounded-preservation assertion (the scenario's own contract-shape tag): read the whole rendered order before and after and compare it, not the two rows under suspicion. The harness's ReadEveryValueRecordedFor is the sibling precedent for asserting a full snapshot rather than a hand-picked field list.

If a Feature has no position at all - a read path that does not number, which the DTO's own comment says is possible - a missing position must not read as "below". Absent is not a position; decide it explicitly and assert the decision.

steps.name: Every Feature in a loop warns and names the others
steps.scenario_name: A loop warns on every Feature in it and names the others
criteria: Both Features in a two-member loop carry a warning naming the other.
The edge that closes the loop is marked as one Lighthouse cannot act on.
A hundred-Feature chain is reported without the read failing or running out of room.
A Feature that lists itself carries the loop warning and names itself.
The loop verdict comes from the same policy the other warnings read; nothing is stored.
steps.implementation_notes:
RED MECHANISM + PARADIGM EXEMPTION: as 01-01.

AC-3.3 / D7 / F-5. Cycles are detected INSIDE the one policy and nothing is stored - a stored cycle flag would be a second source of truth for half the verdict, which is exactly what KPI-5 forbids, and the verdict also depends on the licence and the ordering, neither of which is known at ingestion.

This is the slice's hang prevention, and that is why it lands one epic before anything consumes it. A cycle, like a throughput-less blocker, is what makes Epic #5792's remaining-items loop never terminate. Termination matters more than polish here: a warning that is slightly awkwardly worded costs a support conversation, a missed loop costs a wedged simulation.

FIXTURES ONLY, and this is settled rather than a shortcut. Measured 2026-08-18: Azure DevOps rejects any cycle-closing Predecessor link with TF201035 and the guard is transitive, so #4365 against #5792 and the three-hop #5510, #5511, #5512 chain were both refused. There is no way to dogfood this on ADO at any hop count. Do not spend time trying. Real-data loops arrive with Jira's blocks links (slice 03), with the free-text Portfolio override (slice 04, where nothing guards them), and with a reference that resolves across two Portfolios neither tracker sees whole.

The self-reference case is the one the reconciler's dedup key was chosen for - (FeatureId, ReferenceId), so a Feature listing itself survives dedup and this warning can name it. If it does not surface here, that choice bought nothing.

The hundred-hop clause belongs to the scenario, so assert it at this level too, not only in the detector's unit test: the claim is that a real read of a real payload survives it, and the detector test alone cannot say that.

S3776 on the controller-side assembly of a warning that has to name several other Features. Extract before the third branch.

steps.name: A blocker whose Team has no measured delivery warns
steps.scenario_name: A Feature waiting on one whose Team has no measured delivery is told why
criteria: A Feature waiting on one whose Team has no measured delivery carries a warning.
The warning says the Feature it waits on cannot be forecast, in the instance's own words.
The verdict reuses the existing cannot-be-forecast predicate; no second one is written.
A blocker with no remaining work at all is not reported as unforecastable.
The warning is a distinct kind from cross-Portfolio, ordering and loop.
steps.implementation_notes:
RED MECHANISM + PARADIGM EXEMPTION: as 01-01.

D8's verdict half. The DROP is Epic #5792's and is vacuous until it ships; the WARNING is this slice's. Splitting it this way was deliberate: the verdict is a pure function of data this epic already loads, and stating it now settles the warning vocabulary before any simulation depends on it.

SCENARIO #21 MAPS TO AC-2.3 AND D8, NOT AC-3.6. The slice brief's prerequisite table says "a genuinely unforecastable blocker (D8 / AC-3.6)", and that citation is wrong - AC-3.6 is the terminology criterion ("no warning text contains the word blocked"), which is 04-03's scenario. The delta's own scenario table (row 21) reads "AC-2.3 / D8 verdict half". Use the delta.

REUSED AS IS: Feature.CanBeForecast (Models/Feature.cs:90) and Feature.TeamsWithoutForecast (:96). Read the second comment on that property before writing a test - a Feature with no remaining work is EXEMPT by design, because it carries ForecastService's day-0 sentinel, which has no trials either but is a fact rather than a missing forecast. A test that seeds a done Feature and expects the unforecastable warning is asserting a bug.

This one CAN be dogfooded on real ADO data, and the links were created 2026-08-18 for exactly this: #5511 Task Manager waits on #5733 Opt-In Telemtry, and #5733 has no child Work Items at all. 06-02 confirms it against the running instance.

CA1859 on any new private helper. NUnit2045 on the multi-assert tests.

If the predicate turns out to need a Forecasts collection that the Feature read path does not Include, do NOT widen the Include chain to make a warning work - say so. The read path's cost is 06-01's measurement, and an extra collection Include is the cheapest way to fail it after the fact. S8733 also fires on a second collection Include and is a false positive here, because split queries are configured globally - suppress narrowly, never add .AsSplitQuery().

steps.name: The Depends On cell opens the list
steps.scenario_name: Opening the list of Features one is waiting on
criteria: Clicking a cell that carries a count opens a dialog listing each Feature waited on.
Each row shows name, state, Portfolios, a link that opens the tracker record, and where it was read from.
A withheld row appears with its reason and nothing else about the Feature.
A cell with no count opens nothing; there is no empty dialog to land in.
Every noun renders through getTerm; nothing in the dialog says blocked.
steps.implementation_notes:
RED MECHANISM: on the frontend the equivalent of RED-by-skip is a skipped Vitest case, un-skipped as the component lands; on Playwright it is test.fixme, removed once the spec passes locally. PARADIGM EXEMPTION as 01-01.

This step carries the SAME scenario name as 02-01 on purpose, and the DISTILL Driving Adapter Coverage table is why: scenarios #12 to #16 are listed against BOTH the new route and the dependency dialog, because each is exercised through its own protocol. 02-01 owns the route half, this owns the rendered half. It is not a duplicate mapping.

D11 and the Reuse Analysis: the pattern comes from the existing work-items dialog (components/Common/WorkItemsDialog/WorkItemsDialog.tsx, props title/items/open/onClose, built on DataGridBase). PATTERN REUSED, not extracted - the two dialogs list different things and share only a shell, so a shared abstraction here would be DRY over structure rather than over knowledge. Follow it; do not refactor it.

The cell has to become a gesture. createDependsOnColumn currently returns a plain span (columns.tsx:144-153, with renderDependsOnCount at :136 deliberately blank for zero). Add the handler the way createActiveWorkColumn(getTeams) and createFeatureOrderingActionsColumn already take collaborators - the factory stays policy-ignorant and takes what it is given. FeatureListDataGrid.tsx already holds featureService from ApiServiceContext and already composes the factory at :100, so the dialog state and the fetch both belong there.

The frontend model is zod-validated: Feature.ts's FeatureSchema is the precedent. Per ci-learnings, use .nullable() rather than .optional() for backend nullable fields that serialise to JSON null, and guard nullable date fields - z.coerce.date() turns null into 1970.

MUI traps that have cost this repo real CI cycles: pair every InputLabel id with the Select's labelId or the label is unreachable from Playwright; MUI strips data-testid from ICONS in production builds, so never build a locator on an icon; getByRole("tooltip") and a shared data-testid both match two elements on a page that already hosts the component - scope to the container.

S7735 (no negated condition in a ternary - it is a pre-commit hook pattern and will hard-block the commit), S3358 (no nested ternaries, including inside template literals), S7770 (pass a single-arg pure function directly), S7764 (globalThis over window). Write the empty case as a positive early return, the way renderDependsOnCount already does.

E2E: extend the EXISTING FeatureDependencies.spec.ts by one gesture and the existing FeaturesPage Page Object - never an inline page.locator() in a spec, and do not add a second spec file. One walking skeleton per flow, and this flow already has one. RUN IT against a running Lighthouse before committing; that is a standing rule, not advice. Note the premium-licence fixture is gitignored and absent in a fresh worktree - import it from the main checkout before any screenshot run.

pnpm test green, pnpm build zero warnings, Biome clean on ./src. If Biome reports formatting on files you never touched, check pnpm biome --version against the pin in package.json before believing it - a stale worktree node_modules invents about twenty findings.

steps.name: The warnings column composes the new kinds beside the two it has
steps.scenario_name: The warnings that already existed are untouched
criteria: The done-with-remaining-work and default-size warnings still render, worded exactly as before.
A dependency warning renders alongside them where one is due.
A Feature with nothing wrong with it still renders the all-clear check.
A Feature whose only dependency is honourable and above it renders no dependency warning.
Each of the four dependency warning kinds is separately reachable and separately worded.
steps.implementation_notes:
RED MECHANISM + PARADIGM EXEMPTION: as 01-01, frontend variant per 04-01.

AC-3.5, and it is a byte-for-byte claim. WarningsIndicator.tsx is additive by construction - it early-returns the green check when both flags are false, then renders each warning independently. Add the new branches in the same shape and DO NOT touch DONE_WITH_REMAINING_WORK_TOOLTIP or the default-size template. The existing WarningsIndicator.test.tsx is the regression surface: it should need extension, never edits to its existing expectations. If an existing expectation has to change, the change is wrong.

The existing valueGetter in createWarningsColumn (columns.tsx:109-111) drives the boolean sort and the column type. It has to learn about dependency warnings too, or a row whose only warning is a dependency sorts as clean - a silent half-fix, because the icon renders and the sort lies.

FOUR kinds, not three: cross-Portfolio (#17), positioned-below (#18), loop-member (#19), cannot-be-forecast (#21). The slice brief says three and undercounts - see 01-01's note. Each needs its own aria-label and its own data-testid in the shape the two existing ones use (warning-done-with-remaining-work, warning-default-feature-size), because a shared test id on a page that hosts the component twice matches two elements.

Every string is composed on the CLIENT from a reason code and a name (SA-16), through getTerm, exactly as defaultSizeTooltip already interpolates workItemsTerm and featureTerm. Never interpolate a term into a pre-built sentence - that passes a default-terminology test and breaks the moment anyone renames.

IFeature gains dependencyWarnings beside dependsOnCount (Feature.ts:31) and FeatureSchema gains the matching entry (:68). Slice 01 established the shape; follow it.

Mutation testing note that applies squarely here: a test comparing a rendered string to the constant it came from is self-satisfying - blanking the constant to an empty string survives. Pin each user-visible warning against a LITERAL at least once. This is the single most common survivor in copy-bearing code.

StrykerJS has been observed leaving @ts-nocheck in 661 files; re-anchor the frontend config and check its explicit include list before trusting a score. A new test file missing from that list means every mutant it covers survives for want of a test RUN, which is indistinguishable from a real gap.

steps.name: No dependency warning uses the word that already names something else
steps.scenario_name: No dependency warning uses the word that already names something else
criteria: Every dependency warning this slice can produce is rendered and none contains the reserved word.
The dialog's own strings are covered by the same assertion, not only the warnings.
The existing meaning of that word, and every place it is already used, are unchanged.
The structural scan covers the two new frontend files, not only the column factory.
Renaming the reserved term in settings changes nothing this slice renders.
steps.implementation_notes:
RED MECHANISM + PARADIGM EXEMPTION: as 01-01.

AC-3.6 / D10. TERMINOLOGY_KEYS.BLOCKED and WorkItem.IsBlocked already name epic #5074's shipped concept, and that term is user-renameable, so two meanings of one word follow the same rename and land side by side on the same row where nobody can tell which one they renamed. This is the rendered-string half; the structural half is the ArchUnitNET scan.

A REAL GAP TO CLOSE, found in the code rather than in the brief: DependencySingleDecisionArchUnitTest.NothingThisEpicAdded_CallsAnythingBlocked currently scans the backend Dependencies namespaces plus ONE frontend file - columns.tsx, via TheDependsOnColumn(). Slice 02's user-facing strings live in WarningsIndicator.tsx and DependencyDialog.tsx, neither of which is in that set. Left as it is, AC-3.6 is guarded on the backend and unguarded exactly where the words a user reads are written. Widen TheSourceThisEpicAdded() to both new frontend files in this step.

Widening that scan will surface a real conflict, and it is not a false positive to suppress: WarningsIndicator.tsx and the grid around it legitimately sit near epic #5074's blocked concept. Scope the scan to the regions this epic added, the way TheDependsOnColumn() already scopes columns.tsx, rather than asserting over a whole shared file and then carving out exceptions.

The scan is case-insensitive and matches substrings, so it catches Blocked, blocker and unblocked. "Blocker" as a domain noun is DDD-1's own vocabulary for the Feature being waited on - decide once whether the ubiquitous language keeps it and, if so, make the rule name the decision instead of quietly allowing a prefix. Do not let the test be the place that decision gets made implicitly.

Use depends on, waiting on, not honoured. Tracker wording is not UI wording: ADO's Predecessor and Jira's "is blocked by" are read, never shown.

Comments: never cite an internal reference. AC-3.6, D10, KPI-5 and ADR-158 mean nothing to someone opening the file cold six months from now - write the reason itself, in plain language, or write nothing. The one exception is a pragma suppression, whose justification goes inline.

NUnit1028: a TestCaseSource provider or any non-[Test] member must be private static, and making it private arms CA1859 in the same edit - give it the concrete return type at the same time.

phases.name: Standing guards and what the operator hears

steps.name: At most one place decides, and it depends on nothing that writes
steps.scenario_name: Exactly one place decides whether a dependency can be acted on
criteria: At most one implementation of the honour policy exists; a second one fails the build.
Only that implementation may depend on the cycle detector.
The policy depends on no repository, no DbContext and no service that writes state.
Every reader of the verdict reads it from that one component, not from a re-derivation.
The rule is appended to the existing architecture file rather than restructuring it.
steps.implementation_notes:
RED MECHANISM + PARADIGM EXEMPTION: as 01-01.

KPI-5 / SA-12, and the rule lands HERE rather than in Epic #5792 - maintainer, 2026-08-17, reversing OQ-4's original answer. The reasoning is worth keeping in view while writing it: the decision this rule guards is written in THIS epic and merely consulted by the other, so deferring the guard would ship the invariant behind nothing but a grep, in the epic that was split off precisely so it could ship alone.

AT MOST ONE, not exactly one. Epic #5792 tightens it when it adds the second consumer. Write the assertion so that tightening is a one-word edit, and say in the rule's own message why it is currently the weaker form - otherwise the next reader will assume it was sloppiness.

The file already exists from slice 01 and is designed to be appended to. It gives you LighthouseArchitecture.Production, the ArchRuleDefinition fluent API, LinesMatching over both a SourceFile and a relative path, TheNamespaceThisEpicOwns as a regex so the rules keep covering whatever the next slice adds, and SourceFile itself. Append; do not restructure. Slice 01's roadmap said in as many words "leave the file shaped so slice 02 appends rather than restructures" - this is that append.

The no-state-writing rule is the one ADR-158 leaves undefended and it matters more than it looks: the two consumers inject different predicates, and a predicate that logs, caches or writes makes the verdict DIFFER between the read path and the forecast path - the exact failure KPI-5 exists to prevent. Express it as a dependency rule over the policy's type, not as a comment.

Three orthogonal layers, and each answers a different question rather than repeating the others: the compiled-assembly rule catches a call however many methods it travels through and even a delegate handed the method; the source scan catches what compiles to no edge at all (assign the object to a dynamic local and the method name becomes a string the runtime looks up, invisible to the assembly reader and plain to the file reader - slice 01 tried exactly that against both rules and only the source scan went red); the acceptance scenarios catch behaviour. Keep all three. import-linter's shape was investigated and rejected upstream: its contracts are import-graph only, with no way to enforce method presence on a class.

Scenario #16's structural half belongs here too - no route in this epic writes a dependency, asserted over the controller's route inventory rather than over a 403. 02-03 carries the behavioural half.

CA1865 is now promoted to warning in .editorconfig and TreatWarningsAsErrors stops it at write time: use the char overload of StartsWith and EndsWith for a single-character prefix or suffix, never the string overload with a StringComparison. That rule was filed against line 130 of this very file on 2026-08-18.

Run the mandatory analyzer sweep (dotnet format analyzers Lighthouse.sln --severity info --verify-no-changes --no-restore) after the LAST change of the slice, not after this step - the CA1865 above was written during a review-fix pass, after every step had already swept clean, so every individual check was green and the slice as a whole was not.

steps.name: Two operator log events, sized against the noise already there
criteria: A detected loop emits one warning-level line naming its members.
Unforecastable blockers emit exactly one line per refresh, carrying a count.
A refresh with no loop and no unforecastable blocker adds no line at all.
No per-edge line is emitted at any level, on any path.
The refresh summary operators already read is still legible in the log around them.
steps.implementation_notes:
RED MECHANISM + PARADIGM EXEMPTION: as 01-01.

Decided at the DISTILL review gate, 2026-08-17, and the SIZING is the decision, not an afterthought. Forge asked for per-edge INFO and it was REJECTED: ForecastService already floods the log on every team update, and per-Feature-per-refresh lines would bury the TeamUpdater update-completed summary operators actually read. One WARN per loop, because a loop is rare and genuinely wrong. One aggregated line per refresh with a count for unforecastable blockers, because they are neither. Both verdicts are already visible to users in the warnings column; these exist so a support conversation can happen from a log rather than from a screenshot.

The honour policy is pure and must stay pure - DDD-4, and 05-01's rule now enforces it. So the logging cannot live in the policy. It lives in a thin caller on the refresh path that asks the policy and reports. Put the call beside the reconcile in WorkItemService, which slice 01 already added to the Component Decomposition table as a composition point (a component's call site is not always a component).

GAP FLAGGED: DependencyRefreshReporter is a new type not named in the DESIGN Component Decomposition table - the table has no row for the operator-log events at all, because they were added at the review gate after DESIGN closed. It is listed here because there is nowhere else the aggregation can live without making the policy impure. Raise it with the architect before writing it rather than after.

DI registration goes in Program.cs beside the reconciler at :1219 - but see 01-03: touching Program.cs forces the full backend Integration suite. If the steps can be sequenced so 01-03's registration line and this one land in the SAME edit, do that and say so; two Program.cs commits mean two full-Integration CI runs for one slice.

The existing harness can read what a refresh logged: DependenciesAcceptanceTest replaces ILoggerFactory with a Serilog sink (CapturedLogs) because Serilog ignores anything added as an ILoggerProvider, and DriveAPortfolioRefresh clears the sink before the refresh so host startup and seeding do not pollute the assertion. ReadProblemsLogged() reads at Error and above - a WARN assertion needs CapturedLogs.AtOrAbove(LogEventLevel.Warning).

S2139: do not log-and-rethrow - the event dispatcher already logs and swallows. S6667: a catch that logs must pass the exception as the FIRST logger argument even when the template interpolates its message; that one is error-severity and breaks the local build.

Never the word blocked in a log message. The ArchUnitNET scan reads this namespace.

phases.name: The measurement, and the day it runs against real data

steps.name: The verdict is worked out from what the page already loaded
steps.scenario_name: The verdict is worked out from what the page already loaded
criteria: The number of database commands the Features read issues does not grow with the number of Features.
The same assertion holds at a small Portfolio and at one the size a real instance carries.
Working the verdicts out stores nothing: the stored edge set is identical before and after the read.
The verdict adds no more than 200 ms to the Features read on the restored :5169 backup.
The measured millisecond figure and the pass-or-fail verdict are written into the slice brief.
steps.implementation_notes:
THIS STEP OWNS THE OQ-6 MEASUREMENT. It is the whole reason the slice has a learning hypothesis, and a hypothesis that passes without a number is not a measurement - write the figure down whichever way it goes.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: this is a measurement plus one structural assertion, not a new behaviour. RED MECHANISM as 01-01 for the structural half.

TWO HALVES, and only one of them is a wall-clock number. The structural half - no per-Feature query at any list size - is the one that can be asserted in CI and the one that actually settles the question, because a wall-clock figure on one machine says nothing about a Portfolio ten times larger. There is a precedent for it in this repository: CountsEveryLookup, a DbCommandInterceptor at SecretCustodyServiceTests.cs:1298, wired through options.AddInterceptors(counter) at :1257. Copy that shape; do not invent a second counting mechanism.

Assert the command count is FLAT across two Portfolio sizes, not that it is below some constant. A constant bound passes an N+1 whose N happens to be small in the fixture, which is exactly the fixture anyone would write.

The threshold and the fallback were both fixed at the review gate BEFORE slice 01 stored anything, which is what makes a failure here a planned branch rather than a migration of shipped data: no more than 200 ms added to the /features read on the :5169 restored backup, and no per-Feature query at any list size. If either fails, the verdict moves to ingestion and becomes a precomputed value on the edge - additive columns, expand-only, generated with the CreateMigration script, never a reshape and never dotnet ef migrations add directly. Slice 01 kept FeatureDependencyReference free of read-model fields precisely so that branch stays additive. Report the branch; do not take it inside this step.

The wall-clock half runs against the :5169 dev instance restored from a real backup - never the checked-in .db, which carries no real history. Do NOT aim anything else at :5169 while measuring: a dev run against it creates a second Data Protection key ring that poisons the backend test suite with about twenty unrelated-looking failures and locks Lighthouse.dll.

Nothing is stored as a result of working the verdicts out (SA-13, F-5). Assert it by reading the stored edge set before and after the read and comparing the whole thing, not by trusting that no write was written.

If the suite goes red across unrelated subsystems while you measure, check whether an analyzer sweep or a build was writing to bin/ in another shell - a failure list spanning Jira write-back, CORS and timezone fixtures is that, not this change. Exactly ten failures confined to ReleaseService are contention, not a regression; re-run that class alone.

steps.name: Real data, screenshots, and the gates before the push
criteria: On :5169, #5510 lists #5511, and #5511 lists #5512 and #5733; #5512 and #5733 still read empty.
#5733 having no child work items produces the cannot-be-forecast warning on #5511's row.
The brief records whether cross-Portfolio ran on a second real Portfolio or on fixtures, and that the loop ran on fixtures.
Screenshots of the dialog and of each warning kind are taken the same day against real data.
All CI-parity gates green before the single slice-boundary push.
steps.implementation_notes:
EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: this step is a dogfood confirmation and a gate, not a test. Every behavioural claim in the slice is already asserted somewhere above; nothing new is proven by a screenshot.

THE REAL ADO LINKS EXIST AND ARE NAMED, created 2026-08-18 for this step: #5510 Sizing Poker waits on #5511 Task Manager, which gives the dialog a blocker that is itself waiting; #5511 waits on both #5512 Gitlab Integration and #5733 Opt-In Telemtry, which gives one Feature two blockers; and #5733 has no child Work Items at all, which is a genuinely unforecastable blocker on real data rather than a fixture. #5512 and #5733 carry only the mirrored Successor link and must still read EMPTY - that keeps slice 01's direction guard under test as the edge set grows, and if either reads a number the direction filter has regressed.

TWO THINGS CANNOT BE DOGFOODED HERE, and the brief asks for an explicit answer on each rather than an implication. The loop (AC-3.3): impossible on ADO at any hop count - TF201035, transitively - so it ran on fixtures and its real-data confirmation moves to slice 03, where Jira's blocks links carry no such guard. Cross-Portfolio (AC-3.1): the :5169 instance has ONE Portfolio today, so decide during this step whether a second one is worth creating there or whether AC-3.1 also ran on fixtures. Write which happened into the verdict section; a blank verdict fails the Definition of Done.

SCREENSHOT MECHANICS that have cost this repo real work: the regen keeps the OLD PNG when the diff is under 0.5%, so delete the file first; a run that wipes the database fails six premium tests and LOSES the PNGs they had already deleted, so exclude the @auth tag; the premium licence fixture is gitignored and absent in a fresh worktree, so import it from the main checkout first; and remove any docs symlink under a project directory before a build, or Biome will reformat the docs tree.

CI-PARITY GATES, all of them, before the one push at the slice boundary:
  - Lighthouse.Frontend: pnpm test green; pnpm build zero errors AND zero warnings; pnpm biome check ./src clean.
  - Lighthouse.Backend: dotnet build zero warnings under TreatWarningsAsErrors; dotnet test all NUnit suites green.
  - cd Lighthouse.Backend && dotnet format analyzers Lighthouse.sln --severity info --verify-no-changes --no-restore - MANDATORY and run LAST, after the final code change of the slice rather than after the last feature step. This is the only thing that surfaces the INFO diagnostics that fail Sonar's new_violations gate while dotnet build reports zero warnings.
  - When filtering that output to your own files, union git diff --name-only with git status --porcelain - git diff never lists untracked files, so a slice made largely of new files reports clean while its findings sit unread.
  - SonarQube Cloud: no new issues of ANY severity, including INFO and security hotspots, on both the backend and the frontend project. Read the second gate result when two scanners run in one job.
  - Playwright: run FeatureDependencies.spec.ts and its Page Object locally against a running Lighthouse. Never commit a spec or locator you have not run.
  - Stryker per-feature, at least 80% kill rate, non-negotiable on DependencyCycleDetector and DependencyHonourPolicy. Re-anchor both configs first: they are gitignored, the .NET one targets by byte offset and the frontend one by line range, so a stale config silently mutates the wrong code and reports a meaningless score.

Commit gate is NORMAL for this epic (F-10, maintainer 2026-08-16). The no-commit-without-approval rule belongs to Epic #5792 alone. One focused commit per step; push ONCE at the slice boundary with CI green; never push red - skip a not-yet-passing acceptance test and un-skip to resume. If trunk moved under you, stop and report rather than rebasing.

The learning-hypothesis verdict, the OQ-6 number from 06-01, the two fixtures-versus-real-data answers, and the lighthouse-clients no-gate-owed answer all go into the brief in this step. A blank verdict is a Definition of Done failure, not an omission.

walking_skeleton.step: none - slice 01's skeleton already closes this flow

walking_skeleton.note: One walking skeleton per flow. Slice 02 extends that spec and its Page Object by one gesture in 04-01 rather than adding a second spec.

out_of_scope: Any write path. Lighthouse never authors a dependency (D4), so no add, remove, edit or suppress route exists anywhere in this epic.
Any forecast change. The verdict is computed and displayed here and consumed by nothing - every date belongs to Epic #5792.
The premium hint (US-06). There is no premium behaviour to hint at until Epic #5792 ships its first slice.
Jira and Linear ingestion - slice 03. Two live corrections wait there: Jira link types are instance data rather than constants, and D14's Linear row is wrong about the code.
The per-Portfolio dependency-field override and DependencyOverrideAdditionalFieldDefinitionId - slice 04.
Auto-reordering to satisfy a dependency. A blocker positioned below is a warning and nothing else (D12).
Seeding a dependency loop in Azure DevOps. Measured impossible, transitively, on 2026-08-18.
